A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSSA/LSSAR research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V5 reports original language-model training, passkey retrieval, downstream evaluation, ablations, and orbital-simulation results in Section 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V6 retains original empirical results and adds SSMax comparisons, position-interpolation experiments, and adaptive-sharpening evaluations.

M1.justification: The core normalisation and sharpening operations in Eqs. (4)–(5) and Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendices B.2–B.3 add a position-interpolation adaptation and a position-dependent sharpening parameter beyond the training horizon.

E1.justification: FineWeb/FineWeb-Edu language modelling, passkey retrieval, the same downstream benchmarks and LAMBADA, and orbital simulations are retained. New experiments reuse this coverage. The FineWeb-Edu 100B designation further specifies the existing corpus rather than establishing new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Scalable-Softmax (SSMax; Nakanishi, 2025) to the attention comparisons. Existing Softmax, Sigmoid, ReLU, and LSSA/LSSAR entries remain, as do the comparators in retained downstream and physics experiments.

E3.justification: V6 adds 2,000-step continuation runs with position interpolation at 2K, 4K, and 8K, starting from the 1,024-token checkpoint. Adaptive-sharpening evaluation adds five alpha settings. These introduce additional protocols; newly disclosed settings for retained training runs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 add focused analyses of compatibility with position interpolation and the validation-loss versus retrieval effects of adaptive sharpening. Existing decomposition ablations, activation comparisons, fixed-p sweeps, scaling analyses, attention maps, and planetary cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report passkey accuracy averaged over 100 random-placement trials; the new PI table also uses 100 trials. Neither introduces training-seed replication, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. Table 1 adds SSMax, which becomes best at 1K with loss 3.1705. New PI runs report 8K loss 3.1638 and 21% retrieval accuracy; Appendix B.3 reports 16K loss 3.31 with adaptive alpha=0.1 versus fixed-p 3.45. These are additional configuration-dependent outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.2 corrects v5's unconditional one-hot limit: v6 establishes that nonmaximal entries vanish while t tied maxima each receive limiting mass 1/t. Existing Appendix A derivations, including the gradient analysis, are retained.

C1.justification: The central attention, extrapolation, and downstream-performance claims remain. The fourth introductory contribution and conclusion narrow physical-law recovery to inverse-square structure, and the conclusion drops its emphasis on outperforming the Oracle's fitted constant. The abstract retains broader physical-world-model wording.

C2.justification: V6 substantially qualifies interpretation: Section 3.4 acknowledges the 31.6% fitted-coefficient error, and the Discussion restricts extrapolation and scaling conclusions to tested settings. A new Limitations section addresses model scale, production training, quadratic complexity, and untested deeper networks. Earlier assurances of optimised attention efficiency become explicitly unverified feasibility arguments.

D1.justification: V6 adds a code-availability link and documents optimiser parameters, learning-rate schedules, warmup, clipping, batching, accumulation, and AMP/bfloat16 precision. It also supplies scale-specific training settings and PI finetuning details. These fill substantial reproducibility gaps in v5 without establishing changes to retained runs.

R1.justification: V6 adds the SSMax citation and reference. Related Work also adds a substantive distinction between the already-cited FlattenTransformer's amplification of query-key features in linear attention and LSSAR's sharpening of exact pairwise attention scores.

P1.justification: V6 adds a standalone Limitations section, renames the physical-law section, rewrites selected explanatory and interpretive passages, and expands appendix navigation. Affiliations, acknowledgements, and proceedings information also change. Most prose and the overall organisation remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a smaller single-column display. Table 1 gains group headings and an SSMax row, while Table 3 revises its heading and caption. Two PI tables and an adaptive-sharpening figure are added; existing plots, attention maps, and planetary panels are retained and reflowed.

improvement.justification: V6 improves reproducibility, corrects the tied-maximum argument, and better acknowledges coefficient error and implementation overhead. The added comparisons and supplementary experiments provide useful evidence. The overall gain remains limited: PI is combined with extra finetuning without a matching finetuning-only control, and the abstract retains broader physical-law claims than the revised discussion.
